name: what-i-say
title: What I Actually Say
kicker: Dictation, through /remote-control · AI in the loop, in practice
html:
What I Actually Say

Mostly, I talk. Speech-to-text, into a phone, through /remote-control.

I Own the Goal

One sentence, said out loud.

I Don’t Approve Every Step

The hooks hold the order while nobody watches.

I Read the Record Afterward

Which scenario, which red run, which green run, which commit.

/remote-control

Please give me an update

Red run logged: 3 failures, on behavior. Writing the fix.

How’s it going?

Green. Commit gate: TDD order checked.

go deep on bed gates skill

The bdd-gates skill, understood.

Illustrative, not a transcript. The two questions are the real ones. So is “bed gates”.
say: Mostly, I talk. Most evenings it's the same two questions into my phone: 'Please give me an update', and 'How's it going?' Dictation has opinions of its own; it hears 'BDD gates' as 'bed gates' about half the time. Claude knows what I mean, and the gates don't care either way. What I don't do is approve every step. I own the goal, I say it in a sentence, and afterward I read the record: which scenario, which red run, which green run, which commit. People call that AI in the loop: the person in control, the AI in support. So what did months of that produce?

sources.label: Natarajan et al.: Human-in-the-loop or AI-in-the-loop? (arXiv, 2024)
